quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, all of the following are important, except:

options.text: The helmet meets DOT standards.
The helmet looks nice.
The helmet fits snugly.
The helmet has no defects.

questions.correctAnswerText: The helmet looks nice.
questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet DOT standards. It should fit snugly around your head and have no damage like cracks, loose padding, or torn straps. Appearance is not important for safety.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used in emergency stops.
Should only be used when roads are slippery.
Is weaker than the rear brake.
Is safe if you use it correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe if you use it correctly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake, and it is safe to use as long as you apply it properly.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Only protects your eyes.
Protects your entire face.
Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects your entire face.
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes, not the rest of your face. A windshield is not a substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: When an operator's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, the operator is:

options.text: About to turn left.
About to stop.
About to turn right.
About to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: About to turn right.
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals to show turns and stops when turn signals are not available. A left arm bent at the elbow and pointing upward means the rider is turning right or changing lanes to the right.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle best, a rider should:

options.text: Sit with arms fully extended.
Use arms to hold their body up.
Keep knees away from the gas tank.
Keep feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not your body weight. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handgrips. Press your knees against the gas tank and keep your feet firmly on the footrests for better balance.

questions.question: To make room for drivers merging from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Stay in your lane.
Move to another lane if you can.
Not worry about it since they are merging.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane if you can.
questions.explanation: Drivers may not see your motorcycle when merging. Give them plenty of space to merge safely by changing lanes when possible.

questions.question: The shortest and safest stops happen when:

options.text: You use only the rear brake.
You use only the front brake.
The front tire locks up.
You use both the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: The shortest and safest stops happen when you use both brakes smoothly and evenly without locking either tire.

questions.question: Alcohol impairs your riding ability:

options.text: Well before you reach the legal limit.
Once you reach the legal limit.
Just after the legal limit.
Well above the legal limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Well before you reach the legal limit.
questions.explanation: Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol. Drinking impairs your riding skills well before reaching the legal limit.

questions.question: The rear brake control is usually found:

options.text: On the right handlebar.
On the left handlebar.
Near the left foot.
Near the right foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right foot.
questions.explanation: The rear brake is operated with your right foot.

questions.question: At a blind intersection with a stop sign, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the sign then proceed through.
Ignore the sign and move forward for a better look.
Stop at the sign, move forward slightly to see traffic, and stop again.
Proceed without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the sign, move forward slightly to see traffic, and stop again.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, first stop where the stop sign is located. Then edge forward and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around any buildings, parked cars, or bushes. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help protect you from serious injury?

options.text: A DOT-approved helmet.
Face or eye protection.
Ear buds.
Protective clothing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ear buds.
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high and sturdy boots or shoes that cover your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle, what is the best way?

options.text: Allow one rider to fully pass before another rider begins to pass.
Allow several riders to pass the other vehicle at the same time.
Have the last rider wave to signal no other motorcycles are coming.
Pass in a staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow one rider to fully pass before another rider begins to pass.
questions.explanation: Riders in a group should pass one at a time. Each rider must finish passing and return to their position in the group before the next rider begins to pass.

questions.question: What is true about the front brake on a motorcycle?

options.text: It provides less than half of the motorcycle's braking power.
It provides about 70 percent of the motorcycle's braking power.
It should only be used when the road is wet.
It should be the only brake you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: It provides about 70 percent of the motorcycle's braking power.
questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What formation should a group of motorcyclists use when going through a curve?

options.text: Staggered formation.
Single-file formation.
Side-by-side formation.
Use both lanes if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Although staggered formation is normally best, riders should switch to single-file when taking curves, making turns, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: What does eye contact with another driver really mean?

options.text: The driver sees you.
The driver will not necessarily yield to you properly.
The driver will definitely yield to you properly.
The driver might become angry.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver will not necessarily yield to you properly.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to know that a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but still fail to see them.

questions.question: What do experienced riders do with their lane position?

options.text: Change position within their lane as conditions change.
Stay in one part of the lane at all times.
Weave within the lane to be more visible.
Stay only on the oily part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change position within their lane as conditions change.
questions.explanation: A motorcyclist has three lane position options in their travel lane. Pick whichever position is safest based on the road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: What should you do with your head and eyes when going through a turn on a motorcycle?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn by turning only your head. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help with balance. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handlebars.

questions.question: What lane position is best?

options.text: One that gives you less space and helps you be seen.
One that gives you more space and helps you be seen.
One that puts you near road hazards and lets others pass easily.
One that keeps you close to the vehicle ahead and away from hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that gives you more space and helps you be seen.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that gives you more space and helps others see you. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should prevent other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medications usually affect you?

options.text: They make you drowsy.
They make you more alert.
They make you hungry.
They make you unable to concentrate.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: Most drugs for headaches, colds, hay fever, allergies, or anxiety can make you drowsy and harm your ability to ride safely. Know how any medication affects you before riding.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning sign
Service sign
Regulatory sign
Speed limit sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.
